what_it_does: This paper presents a Class-D audio amplifier—a highly efficient amplifier chip for speakers—that uses a novel voltage-boosting technique to overcome a fundamental trade-off. Normally, audio amplifiers powered by batteries are limited in maximum output power by the battery voltage. Previous attempts to boost the voltage either used inefficient two-stage converters (losing 20% of power as heat) or compromised dynamic range (the ability to accurately reproduce very soft and very loud sounds simultaneously). This design uses double-sided voltage-boosting modulation that integrates a feedback amplifier with a simplified single-stage power converter, achieving 87% efficiency and a dynamic range of 121 dB—competitive with high-end systems—while needing only one off-chip inductor.
